MEMORANDUM - SPA REPRESENTATIONS vs. DILIGENCE FINDINGS (PrecisionFlow / Cascadia)
To: Buyer deal team. Basis: Seller draft SPA Arts. III-V (3/14/25), Seller draft Disclosure Schedules, H&F diligence report and IP memo (3/10/25), Ridgeline email chain and workpaper, contract summary. Articles I-II and VI-XII (indemnity, governing law, closing conditions) were NOT supplied; recommendations assume they are negotiable. Facts are as of March 2025; if reading later, bring everything down to the current date.

1. BOTTOM LINE
Schedules do not track the SPA and conflict with each other and with diligence on shares, lenders, patents, insurance and real property. Do not sign until Tier 1 items are resolved or protected by closing conditions, special indemnities/escrow and price changes.

2. DISCREPANCY MAP (CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW)

CRITICAL
C1. Share title / Karen Beecham (SPA 3.3(d); Sched. 3.2 says "free and clear"). 2021 divorce decree gives ex-wife claim to 5% of Hal's shares (3.1% of company; about $8.9M). Seller counsel says disputed; no order produced. Hal's January board presentation disclosed no encumbrance. Action: closing condition of court order or signed release (add Karen as party if needed); special escrow of about $8.9M; remove "Permitted Encumbrances" leakage for Shares; Seller-counsel opinion. Consider delaying signing (Ridgeline view).
C2. Capitalization conflict (SPA 3.3(a)-(b) vs Sched. 3.2). SPA: 1,000,000 shares outstanding, par $0.01, Hal 620,000. Schedule: 5,000,000 shares, par $0.001, Hal 3,100,000. Percentages match, but per-share allocation, stock certificates and RSAs must be reconciled. Also SPA 3.3(e) says RSAs are the only shareholder agreements, yet Sched. 3.15/3.4 disclose a 2016 Investors' Rights Agreement (tag/drag, board observer, notice rights) and Sched. 3.2 says no voting agreements. Rep 3.3(e) is false as drafted. Action: stock ledger audit; certificate; IRA terminated or waived at closing; fix reps.
C3. Kessler change-of-control termination (SPA 3.15(a)(iv); Sched. 3.15 silent). MSA s.12.3 lets Kessler terminate on 60 days' notice after acquisition of >50%; Kessler is $29.4M (20.6%) of revenue; confirmed by contract summary and workpaper.  Action: Kessler written waiver as closing condition; schedule correction; retention escrow/earn-out or price holdback; rep that no customer has indicated termination or reduction.
C4. NorthPoint MSA expired 2/28/25 (SPA 3.15(c) "in full force"; Sched. 3.15 lists it as current term expiring 2/28/25). $18.6M (13%); no renewal; contract summary also shows 90-day termination for convenience and no auto-renewal. Action: executed renewal as closing condition; revise rep; consider price/earn-out protection. Combined Kessler+NorthPoint = 33.6% of revenue.
C5. Monterrey lease consent omitted from Schedule 5.3 / SPA 5.3 (and 3.2(c)(iii) no-conflict rep). Lease requires landlord consent to direct or indirect change of control (cited as s.14.2 by H&F, s.8.4 in contract summary; 60 days' prior notice; default permits termination on 30 days' notice). Monterrey is $38.2M (26.7%) of revenue. Action: add to Required Consents; start notice immediately (60-day notice cannot be met if consent is sought late); make landlord consent a closing condition. Reconcile the section cite.
C6. Environmental REC omitted (SPA 3.12(a),(c); Sched. 3.12). Oct. 2024 Phase I (Greenleaf) found historic chlorinated-solvent REC at Dayton NE corner and recommended Phase II; not scheduled; Seller offered no support. SPA 3.12(c) says all reports delivered. A stock buyer inherits CERCLA/Ohio liabilities of the owner-operator (the Company); no landowner defense is available to a buyer of stock. Action: Phase II pre-signing or pre-closing; Schedule correction; environmental indemnity (uncapped or separate cap, long survival) plus escrow; PLL policy (known conditions will be excluded, so price/indemnity must carry it).
C7. Dayton real property status conflict (SPA 3.7(a), Sched. 3.18, H&F title search: owned in fee) vs key-contract-summary OC-010 (Dayton HQ leased from Clearwater Industrial Properties, $1.44M/yr, through 12/31/27). Both cannot be true; if there is a lease, rep 3.7(a), Sched. 3.15 and ABL mortgage collateral are wrong. Action: pull title commitment, deed, lease; correct 3.7 and 3.15.

HIGH
H1. Patents (SPA 3.9(a); Sched. 3.9). Two PF-4200 patents (10,891,234; 10,891,235) omitted. Further: none of the 12 scheduled patent numbers (for example 8,123,456) matches the 14 USPTO-verified numbers in the IP memo (for example 8,214,703), and titles, dates and pending-application numbers (Sched.: 17/456,789 etc.; IP memo: 17/482,116, 17/639,504, 18/201,338) differ. Schedule also lists a second trademark (Reg. 4,012,567) not found by H&F. SPA text says "twelve" patents - must read fourteen. Action: replace schedule with USPTO-verified list; assignment chain-of-title search; IP title/validity as fundamental-type rep; rep 3.9(b) validity should not be knowledge-qualified.
H2. AquaDyne (SPA 3.9(c); Sched. 3.8/3.9). Hargrove & Lind opinion does not cover claim 14 (H&F report) or claims 14-22 (IP memo) - the sources conflict on scope; obtain the opinion itself. Seller withheld PF-4200 test data. PF-4200 is about $22M (15%) of revenue per management. 3.9(c) "believes without merit" and the rep that the opinion supports it are misleading by omission; willfulness exposure (35 U.S.C. 284). Action: data production and supplemental opinion as closing condition; specific AquaDyne indemnity outside basket/cap with escrow; add rep 3.9(c) covers non-infringement of all claims; disclose limitation in the Schedule.
H3. Tax - California (SPA 3.14(a),(b),(i); Sched. 3.10/3.14 lists only five states). San Jose employee since 1/2022; about $3.8M CA sales; no CA returns. H&F states nexus is "clear"; qualify this: P.L. 86-272 (15 U.S.C. 381) may bar CA net-income tax if activity is limited to solicitation of orders for tangible goods, but a filing requirement and the $800 minimum franchise tax still apply if "doing business" (R&TC 23101; FTB guidance), and payroll withholding/EDD registration, sales/use tax and any non-solicitation activity (service, installation) must be checked. Exposure H&F estimates $100-300K+ plus 25% penalty and interest; likely low-seven figures at worst.  Action: CA tax counsel; voluntary disclosure agreement pre-closing; pre-closing tax indemnity, first-dollar, separate from basket; fix 3.14(i).
H4. Debt/lender identity and terms (SPA 3.15(b)(viii)-(x), 5.3; Sched. 3.4/3.7/5.3). Four names for the ABL lender: Heartland Commercial Bank (SPA), Meridian National Bank (Schedules), First Midwestern Bank (H&F), Midwestern Commercial Bank (workpaper), Keystone National Bank (IP memo), Dayton Industrial Bank (contract summary). Term lender: Heartland / Great River Equipment Finance / Dayton Industrial Bank. Dates, maturities and terms conflict (ABL 5/15/2020 maturing 5/15/2025 per Schedule - before the 6/30/25 closing - vs. A&R 7/1/2023 maturing 6/30/2028 per contract summary; Terraverde note: 6.5%, maturity 6/30/2026, dated 2016 per Schedule vs. 8% PIK, dated 1/15/2018, maturing 1/14/2028 with mandatory COC prepayment and accrued PIK per contract summary; term loan maturity 9/1/2027 vs 9/30/2027). Payoff letters and consents go to the wrong party if uncorrected; the $34.2M indebtedness figure omits accrued PIK, prepayment amounts and a possible ABL maturity default. Action: obtain executed credit documents and payoff letters; fix schedules; define Indebtedness to include accrued interest, PIK, breakage, guaranty release.
H5. Martinez / insurance (SPA 3.10(c), 3.13). Rep that all litigation is "adequately covered" is contradicted: $12M demand vs $10M per-occurrence limit; reservation of rights covers punitive damages. SPA 3.13(b)(v) says a $15M Continental Excess umbrella exists; Sched. 3.13 says "Umbrella: None"; H&F and the policy review list none. If no umbrella, gap is at least $2M.  Contract summary shows CGL expired 12/31/24 with renewal "pending", contradicting rep of coverage through 12/31/25; the policy requires post-COC notice and permits non-renewal. Ohio caps punitive damages at 2x compensatory (R.C. 2315.21) and R.C. 3937.182 limits insuring them. Action: confirm umbrella existence; bring-down certificates; defense counsel merits/settlement report; Martinez special indemnity/escrow (at least $2M plus punitive); correct 3.10(c), 3.13(d).
H6. EBITDA add-back (SPA 3.4(e) rep that each adjustment is non-recurring and appropriate). $0.60M COVID add-back: similar charges $0.55M (FY22) and $0.45M (FY23); HHS ended the emergency 5/11/23. Ridgeline JE detail (3/6) says only about $0.22M (inventory write-down) is arguably one-time, so the defensible add-back is up to $0.22M, not zero: adjusted EBITDA $29.83M x 9.5 = about $283.4M (-$3.6M); full rejection gives $29.61M/$281.3M (-$5.7M). H&F report still shows the full $5.7M - conform to the later email. Action: price negotiation; delete 3.4(e) adjustments rep or treat as a flat rep (rep supports an indemnity claim at multiple); tighten "EBITDA" definition (Section 2.5(b) not supplied).
H7. Pension (SPA 3.16(e)). $4.3M unfunded per Jan. 2024 valuation; Buyer actuary $6.8M at 12/31/24 (discount rate 5.4% to 4.6%): +$2.5M. Actuary identity conflicts: Millbrook (SPA), Cornerstone (Schedule), Clarkfield (workpaper). Workpaper and H&F cite the wrong SPA section (3.17(d)). Action: bring-down valuation within 60 days of closing with dollar-for-dollar adjustment or debt-like treatment; confirm 412/PBGC funding status; correct actuary.

MEDIUM
M1. Working capital. Target $18.4M "TTM average" vs workpaper quarterly NWC 16.9/20.3/25.1/29.8 (simple average about $23.0M). Dec. 31 NWC $29.8M implies an $11.4M upward payment to Seller; peg appears understated and unverified; inventory +21.6% vs revenue +8.7% suggests aging. Action: audit monthly calculations; reset peg to normalized level; inventory reserve review. (Section 2.5 not supplied.)
M2. OSHA (SPA 3.11(a),(c); Sched. 3.6/3.14). October 2024 lockout/tagout citation ($28,700, serious) contested before OSHRC. Schedules disclose it (H&F's view that schedule needs correction is partly overtaken), but SPA 3.11(c) text lists only two citations and says all are "fully resolved"; Schedule 3.14 says "Schedule 3.14" is the compliance schedule while SPA numbering calls it 3.11. Action: conform rep text; LOTO program audit; specific indemnity.
M3. Headcount (SPA 3.17(a); Sched. 3.17). 730 vs H&F 740; but the Schedule counts the 75 corporate staff inside Dayton's 485, while H&F counts them separately (485+180+75=740). Monterrey 170 vs 180.  Action: payroll census; reconcile.
M4. Section 382 (SPA 3.14(f)). Schedule 3.10 discloses 382 risk; H&F says the SPA is silent. Quantify: annual limit equals equity value times the long-term tax-exempt rate (3.67% for March 2025) - roughly $9M on a $250M+ equity value, above the $4.1M NOL, so limitation is likely not binding (still subject to the 80% taxable-income cap).

M5. R&D credits: FY23-24 credits ($0.7M) not under exam; seek specific tax indemnity.
M6. Contract schedule completeness (SPA 3.15(a)). Contract summary lists Summit Valve ($5.8M), Bridger Creek ($4.7M; $3M minimum), Hawkins Metal (largest supplier, $6.8M), Clearwater lease, Dunlap $10M minimum, Overland MFN, none on Schedule 3.15; Heartland Tool & Die/Cascade Power in workpaper top-10 also absent. SPA 3.15(a)(i)/(ii) requires all >$1M contracts and MFN/minimum-type contracts. Dates/terms of scheduled customer contracts differ across documents (e.g., Dunlap 6/1/22 vs 6/1/23 vs 9/1/20). Action: full contract list with originals; rep that copies are true.
M7. Verteon: Schedule says non-transferable without consent; contract summary (s.12.1) and H&F say COC carve-out; IP memo says silent. Read license.
M8. Sched. 3.17 says only 8 RSA executives have non-competes; IP memo found 18-month non-competes in engineer agreements. Knowledge group names the CFO as Peretti but Schedule lists Caldwell as CFO; Sandra Cho is VP Operations in SPA but General Counsel elsewhere. Fix Knowledge definition.
M9. CIC plan: $3.01M double-trigger exposure; RSA acceleration single-trigger; treat as price/transaction expense; run 280G.
M10. Schedule numbers do not match SPA sections (e.g., SPA 3.4 Financials vs Schedule 3.4 Consents). Re-number; require section-specific disclosure.
M11. HSR is "if applicable" in drafts; $287M exceeds the 2025 $126.4M threshold, so filing is required (fee tier $105,000); timeline must allow the waiting period.

LOW
L3. IRS exam, transfer pricing (cost-plus 8%), CBA expiry 2/28/26 and Thompson EEOC are properly disclosed, but direction of transfer pricing flow conflicts: SPA says components move Company to Subsidiary; Schedule 3.10 says Monterrey to Dayton. Mexican transfer-pricing rep is flat; the audit emphasis-of-matter makes this a rep worth keeping unqualified.

4. CROSS-CUTTING POINTS
(a) Sandbagging/knowledge. Buyer knows of these breaches. Delaware is pro-sandbagging absent contract language (Arwood v. AW Site Services, Del. Ch. Mar. 9, 2022), but governing law and the indemnity article were not supplied, and the draft 4.7 non-reliance clause and 3.21 "full disclosure" rep interact. Add an express pro-sandbagging clause, and fraud carve-out from non-reliance (ABRY Partners v. F&W, Del. Ch. 2006). Known items are better covered by special indemnities than by rep claims.
(b) Disclosure standard. Schedules should not cure by "reasonably apparent" cross-reference; schedule updates under SPA 5.5 must not cure breaches for indemnity or closing-condition purposes.
(c) Pattern of incomplete disclosure supports fundamental-rep treatment, longer survival and escrow above 8%.
(d) Quantified ask: price effect $3.6-5.7M (EBITDA), $2.5M (pension), NWC peg reset, plus special escrows: title $8.9M, environmental TBD, Martinez at least $2M, AquaDyne TBD, California TBD.

Source documents (credit agreements, Dayton deed/lease, patent records, Hargrove opinion) not available to resolve factual conflicts
